passages.scripture: A few days later Jesus went back to Capernaum. And when the people heard that He was home, they gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room, not even outside the door, as Jesus spoke the word to them.

lines.text: A few days later Jesus went back to Capernaum — Capernaum was a town by the Sea of Galilee where Jesus had taught before.
And the people heard that Jesus was home.
So the people gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room.
There was no more room, not even outside the door — the crowd filled the house and spilled outside the house.
Jesus spoke the word to them — this word is God's message, the good news that His kingdom has come near.

passages.scripture: Then a paralytic was brought to Him, carried by four men.

lines.text: Then a paralyzed man was brought to Jesus.
Four men carried the paralyzed man to Jesus.

passages.scripture: Since they were unable to get to Jesus through the crowd, they uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat.

lines.text: There was a paralyzed man.
The paralyzed man was lying on a mat.
A crowd was around Jesus.
So the four men could not bring the paralyzed man to Jesus.
So the four men uncovered the roof above Jesus.
And the four men made an opening through the roof.
And then the four men lowered the mat down through the opening.

passages.scripture: When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”

lines.text: Jesus saw the faith of the four men — they were so convinced Jesus would heal the paralyzed man that they were willing to overcome obstacles to get him into Jesus’ presence.
Jesus is called the “Everlasting Father” — He cares for His people like a father, so He calls the paralyzed man “son”.
The paralyzed man was not an earthly son of Jesus.
Jesus said to the paralyzed man, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
God forgave the paralyzed man’s sins — by the time Jesus finished speaking, every sin of his was forgiven.

passages.scripture: But some of the scribes were sitting there and thinking in their hearts, “Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”

lines.text: Some of the scribes were sitting there.
The scribes were thinking in their hearts — silently, to themselves.
The scribes thought, “Why does this man — Jesus — speak like this?”
The scribes thought, “Jesus is blaspheming!”
To blaspheme is to insult God — for example, by claiming to do what only God can do.
The scribes thought, “Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
The scribes were right about this: only God can forgive sins — but they did not realize that Jesus Christ is God over all.

passages.scripture: At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves. “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?” He asked.

lines.text: At once Jesus knew what the scribes were thinking within themselves.
Jesus knew it in His spirit — no one told Him, and the scribes had not said a word.
Jesus asked the scribes, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?”
God alone knows the hearts of all people — and Jesus knew what was in every person’s heart, including the scribes’ hearts.

passages.scripture: “Which is easier: to say to a paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?

lines.text: Anyone can say, “Your sins are forgiven” — no one can see whether a person’s sins are forgiven.
But if someone says, “Get up, pick up your mat, and walk,” everyone can see whether the paralyzed man walks — whether or not the person speaking has the power to do a miracle.
Jesus asked the scribes, “Which is easier: to say to a paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?”

passages.scripture: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic, “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”

lines.text: Jesus called Himself the Son of Man — Mary gave birth to Jesus and Mary is ultimately from the man Adam.
Authority on earth to forgive sins means that God has given someone on earth the right and the power to forgive sins.
Jesus said to the scribes, “The Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.”

Jesus wanted the scribes to know that He has authority to forgive sins — if Jesus claims to forgive, and God allows Jesus to do a miracle at the same time, then the miracle is God bearing witness that everything Jesus says is true.
So Jesus said to the paralyzed man, “I tell you, get up.”
Jesus said, “Pick up your mat.”
Jesus said, “And go home.”
If the man got up and walked, everyone could see that Jesus really has authority to forgive sins.

passages.scripture: And immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all. As a result, they were all astounded and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”

lines.text: As soon as Jesus spoke, the paralyzed man was healed and got up.
The man picked up his mat.
The man walked out in front of everyone.
Everyone there saw it — including the scribes.
Everyone was amazed.
Everyone praised God.
The people said, “We have never seen anything like this!”

passages.scripture: Once again Jesus went out beside the sea. All the people came to Him, and He taught them there.

lines.text: Jesus went out of Capernaum again, to the shore of the Sea of Galilee.
The whole crowd kept coming to Jesus.
Jesus kept teaching the crowd.

passages.scripture: As He was walking along, He saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him, and Levi got up and followed Him.

lines.text: As Jesus was walking along, Jesus saw a man named Levi.
Levi was the son of Alphaeus.
Levi was sitting at the tax booth.
Levi’s job was to collect taxes — money that the people had to pay to the rulers.
Jesus said to Levi, “Follow Me.”
Levi got up and followed Jesus.

passages.scripture: While Jesus was dining at Levi’s house, many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Him and His disciples—for there were many who followed Him.

lines.text: Jesus was having a meal at Levi’s house.
A disciple is someone who follows a teacher in order to learn from him.
Here “sinners” means people known for living sinful lives.
Many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Jesus and His disciples.
There were many people following Jesus.

passages.scripture: When the scribes who were Pharisees saw Jesus eating with these people, they asked His disciples, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

lines.text: The Pharisees were a group of Jews who were very strict about keeping God’s law and their own traditions.
Some of the scribes were Pharisees.
The scribes who were Pharisees saw Jesus eating with tax collectors and sinners.
Tax collectors were known for being corrupt — collecting more money than they ought, to make themselves richer — so many people looked down on tax collectors.
Eating a meal with someone was a sign of friendship.
The scribes asked Jesus’ disciples, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

passages.scripture: On hearing this, Jesus told them, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

lines.text: Jesus heard what the scribes asked.
Jesus said to the scribes, “Healthy people do not need a doctor, but sick people do.”
Righteous people are people who do what is right.
Jesus called people to follow Him, just as Jesus called Levi.
Jesus said, “I have not come to call righteous people, but sinners.”
Just as sick people need doctors, sinners need Jesus.
Sinners who mistakenly judge themselves as righteous don’t yet realize they need Jesus.

passages.scripture: Now John’s disciples and the Pharisees were often fasting. So people came to Jesus and asked, “Why don’t Your disciples fast like John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees?”

lines.text: To fast means to go without food for a time, often to pray and seek God.
The disciples of John the Baptist were fasting, and the Pharisees were fasting too.
Some people came to Jesus.
The people asked Jesus, “Why do the disciples of John and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but Your disciples do not fast?”

passages.scripture: Jesus replied, “How can the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them? As long as He is with them, they cannot fast.

lines.text: A bridegroom is a man who is getting married.
At a wedding, the bridegroom’s guests celebrate with him — a wedding is a time of joy, not a time of fasting.
Jesus replied, “How can the guests of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them?”
Jesus said, “As long as the bridegroom is with them, the guests cannot fast.”
Jesus spoke of Himself as the bridegroom.
Jesus spoke of His disciples as the guests.
While Jesus was with His disciples, it was a time of joy for them, not a time of fasting.

passages.scripture: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.

lines.text: Jesus said, “But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from the guests.”
Jesus said, “Then, on that day, the guests will fast.”
Jesus was speaking of the day He would be taken away from His disciples — the day Jesus would be put to death and the day Jesus would leave earth to go back to heaven.
When Jesus was taken away, His disciples would be full of sorrow, and they would fast.

passages.scripture: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. If he does, the new piece will pull away from the old, and a worse tear will result.

lines.text: A patch is a piece of cloth sewn over a hole to fix it.
New cloth that has never been washed is “unshrunk” — when unshrunk cloth gets wet, it shrinks and gets smaller.
Jesus said, “No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment.”
Jesus said, “If someone does, the new patch will pull away from the old garment, and the tear will become worse.”
Jesus brings something new, and the new does not fit into the old ways.

passages.scripture: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.”

lines.text: A wineskin is a bag made from animal skin, used to hold wine.
New wine is still changing — new wine gives off gas, and the gas makes the wineskin stretch.
An old wineskin has already stretched and become stiff, so an old wineskin cannot stretch any more.
Jesus said, “No one pours new wine into old wineskins.”
Jesus said, “If someone does, the wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the wineskins will be ruined.”
Jesus said, “Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.”
The teaching of Jesus being received by His disciples is like new wine in new wineskins.
The teaching of Jesus being given to people stuck in their ways and traditions is like new wine poured into old wineskins.

passages.scripture: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain as they walked along.

lines.text: A grainfield is a field where grain, like wheat, grows.
One Sabbath, Jesus was walking through the grainfields.
The heads of grain are the tops of the grain plants, where the seeds that people eat grow.
As the disciples of Jesus walked along, the disciples began to pick heads of grain.

passages.scripture: So the Pharisees said to Him, “Look, why are they doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”

lines.text: The Pharisees saw the disciples of Jesus picking grain on the Sabbath.
God’s law said that no one should work on the Sabbath.
But God’s law allowed people walking through a neighbor’s field to pick grain by hand.
However, the Pharisees considered picking grain to be harvesting, and harvesting was work.
So the Pharisees said to Jesus, “Look, why are Your disciples doing what is not allowed on the Sabbath?”

passages.scripture: Jesus replied, “Have you never read what David did when he and his companions were hungry and in need?

lines.text: David was a man God chose to be king of Israel, about a thousand years before Jesus.
The Pharisees studied God’s written word closely, so the Pharisees had read about David.
Jesus answered the Pharisees with a question.
Jesus said, “Have you never read what David did when David and his companions were hungry and in need?”

passages.scripture: During the high priesthood of Abiathar, he entered the house of God and ate the consecrated bread, which was lawful only for the priests. And he gave some to his companions as well.”

lines.text: In David’s time, the house of God was a tent where the people of Israel worshiped God — the temple building had not yet been built.
Priests were men who served God at the house of God.
The high priest was the leader of all the priests.
The consecrated bread was holy bread — twelve loaves set out before God in the house of God each week.
God’s law said only the priests could eat the consecrated bread.
However, David and his men were not priests.
Jesus said, “In the time of Abiathar the high priest, David went into the house of God and ate the consecrated bread.”
Jesus said, “David also gave some of the consecrated bread to the men with David.”

passages.scripture: Then Jesus declared, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.

lines.text: Jesus said to the Pharisees, “The Sabbath was made for people.”
Jesus said, “People were not made for the Sabbath.”
God made the Sabbath as a gift to people — a day for people to rest and worship God.
God’s rules about the Sabbath were meant to help people, not to harm people.
